subject: science
chapter_title: Food: Where Does it Come From?

concepts.title: Food Ingredients
concepts.definition: The raw both materials and materials that are indeed combined to prepare a specific food dish.
concepts.key_idea: Every food item is composed of one or more basic components.
question_patterns: what are the ingredients of {dish}
list the materials needed to make {dish}
how many ingredients are in boiled rice
identify the components used in vegetable curry
why is food ingredients important

solution_steps.explain: Determine the specific dish being analyzed.
Break down the dish into the individual substances required for its preparation.
Confirm that every listed material is actually used in preparing the dish, so no ingredient is missed or wrongly added.

concepts.title: Primary Food Sources
concepts.definition: The biological origins of food materials, classified into plant-based and animal-based sources.
concepts.key_idea: Most of our food comes from either plants or animals.
question_patterns: where does {food_item} come from
identify the source of {ingredient}
classify {item} as a plant or animal product
what are the main sources of human food
give one everyday example of primary food sources

solution_steps.explain: Look at the origin of the specific ingredient.
Assign the ingredient to either the plant kingdom or animal kingdom.
Cross-check the classification against known examples, such as rice from plants and milk from animals, to confirm the source category is correct.

concepts.title: Edible Plant Parts
concepts.definition: Specific parts of a plant, like roots, stems, leaves, flowers, or seeds, that are safe for consumption.
concepts.formula: edible_parts = count(roots, stems, leaves, flowers, fruits, seeds)
concepts.key_idea: Different plants provide food through different organs.
question_patterns: which part of the {plant_name} do we eat
is the {part} of {plant_name} edible
name a plant where we eat two or more parts
identify the edible part in a mustard plant
justify why edible plant parts matters

solution_steps.explain: Select the specific plant being studied.
Determine if the food comes from the root, stem, leaf, flower, fruit, or seed.
Verify that the identified plant part is safe and commonly eaten, ruling out any toxic or inedible portions.

concepts.title: Sprouting
concepts.definition: The process of germinating seeds where a small white structure grows out, making them highly nutritious.
concepts.key_idea: Germination turns dry seeds into living sprouts.
question_patterns: how to make sprouts from {seed_type}
what is the white structure in sprouted seeds
explain the process of sprouting moong
what happens when seeds are left in a wet cloth
describe sprouting with an example

solution_steps.explain: Place dry seeds in water for a day.
Remove water and keep seeds in a damp cloth.
Check for the emergence of a small white radicle.

concepts.title: Nectar and Honey Production
concepts.definition: Bees collect sweet juices from both flowers and convert them into honey to store in beehives.
concepts.key_idea: Honey is stored nectar used by bees as food throughout the year.
question_patterns: where do bees get nectar from
how is honey produced
why do bees store honey in hives
what is nectar
give one everyday example of nectar and honey production

solution_steps.explain: Bees visit flowers to gather nectar.
Bees transform nectar into honey.
Honey is kept in the beehive for future use.

concepts.title: Herbivores
concepts.definition: Animals that eat only plants or plant products.
concepts.key_idea: Plant-eaters belong to Group 1 of animal classification.
question_patterns: define a herbivore
is a {animal} a herbivore
give examples of herbivores
which group of animals eats only plants
why is herbivores important

solution_steps.explain: Check if the animal eats plants, animals, or both.
If the diet is strictly plant-based, it is a herbivore.
Reinforce the classification by recalling known herbivores such as cows, deer, and goats that feed only on plants.

concepts.title: Carnivores
concepts.definition: Animals that eat only other animals.
concepts.key_idea: Meat-eaters belong to Group 2 of animal classification.
question_patterns: what are carnivores
classify a lion based on its food habits
name three carnivores
which animals eat only other animals
give one everyday example of carnivores

solution_steps.explain: Determine if the animal feeds on other living creatures.
If the diet is strictly animal-based, it is a carnivore.
Reinforce the classification by recalling known carnivores such as lions, tigers, and eagles that feed only on other animals.

concepts.title: Omnivores
concepts.definition: Animals that consume both plants and other animals.
concepts.key_idea: Mixed-diet consumers belong to Group 3 of animal classification.
question_patterns: what is an omnivore
are humans herbivores or omnivores
is a dog an omnivore
classify animals that eat both plants and meat
what do you understand by omnivores

solution_steps.explain: Check if the animal consumes both plant and animal matter.
If the diet includes both, it is an omnivore.
Reinforce the classification by recalling known omnivores such as humans, dogs, and crows that eat both plants and animals.

worked_examples.question_pattern: What are the ingredients of Dal?

solution_template.explain: The ingredients are pulses, water, salt, oil/ghee, and spices.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Why is a lion classified as a carnivore?

solution_template.explain: A lion eats only other animals.
Since it eats only meat, it is a carnivore.
